library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
PKNCA::PKNCA.options(progress = FALSE)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zyryanov_2023_meropenem"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zyryanov_2023_meropenem"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2023.1079680> (open access)

# Population

Zyryanov 2023 retrospectively analysed routine therapeutic drug monitoring
(TDM) of meropenem in 66 preterm newborns treated in the intensive care unit of
City Clinical Hospital 24, Moscow, between January 2018 and February 2022. Each
patient contributed one TDM occasion: a peak within 30 min after dosing and a
trough just before the next dose (132 concentrations, HPLC-UV, LLOQ 0.2 mg/L).
Meropenem was given empirically at 40-120 mg/kg/day as 1-3 h IV infusions two or
three times a day (20-40 mg/kg per dose every 8-12 h); the daily dose at TDM was
94.6 +/- 40.4 mg/day.

Table 1 (mean +/- SD, median): gestational age 28.9 +/- 2.93 weeks (28.5),
postnatal age at TDM 33.0 +/- 20.88 days (30.5), postconceptual age 33.6 +/-
3.69 weeks (33.6), weight 1.66 +/- 0.464 kg (1.58, IQR 1.30-2.04), height 38.3
+/- 4.26 cm, serum creatinine 46.66 +/- 20.235 umol/L, Schwartz GFR 27.31 +/-
9.676 mL/min/1.73 m^2; 39.4% female. Diagnoses included pneumonia (84.8%),
necrotizing enterocolitis (60.6%) and bacterial meningitis (9.1%).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Zyryanov_2023_meropenem")$population`.

# Source trace

Per-parameter origins are also recorded inline in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Zyryanov_2023_meropenem.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Structure: one compartment, zero-order input, first-order elimination, parameterised by Kel and V | -- | Methods, 'PK analysis' |
| `cl = kel * vc`, `t1/2 = 0.693 / kel` (derived) | -- | Methods, 'PK analysis' |
| `lkel` | log(0.30) 1/h | Results and Abstract: Kel 0.31 +/- 0.13 (median 0.3) |
| `lvc` | log(1.2) L | Results and Abstract: V 1.2 +/- 0.4 (median 1.2) |
| `etalkel` | log(0.42^2 + 1) = 0.1624 | Results: Kel CV 42% |
| `etalvc` | log(0.33^2 + 1) = 0.1033 | Results: V CV 33% |
| `propSd`, `addSd` | fixed(0) | Methods: weighting by the inverse assay variance; coefficients not reported |
| Unbound fraction for PK/PD targets | 0.98 | Methods, 'PD analysis' |
| Derived medians used as checks | T1/2 2.33 h, CL 0.355 L/h, V 0.76 L/kg, CL 0.219 L/h/kg | Table 2 |

# Typical-value check against Table 2

Table 2 summarises the individual Bayesian posterior half-lives and clearances.
Their medians follow directly from the median Kel and V, which is why the
medians (rather than the means 0.31 1/h and 1.2 L) are the typical values in the
model file. Weight-normalised values use the Table 1 median weight of 1.58 kg.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Zyryanov_2023_meropenem")
ini_df <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$iniDf
theta <- setNames(ini_df$est, ini_df$name)
kel_tv <- exp(theta[["lkel"]])
v_tv <- exp(theta[["lvc"]])
wt_med <- 1.58

typical <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("T1/2 (h)", "CL (L/h)", "V (L/kg)", "CL (L/h/kg)"),
  Model = c(log(2) / kel_tv, kel_tv * v_tv, v_tv / wt_med, kel_tv * v_tv / wt_med),
  `Table 2 median` = c(2.33, 0.355, 0.76, 0.219)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(`% diff` = round(100 * (Model / `Table 2 median` - 1), 1))
knitr::kable(typical, digits = 3)

# The model is a reparameterisation of the same two numbers Table 2 is
# derived from, so these agree to within the rounding of the printed values.
stopifnot(all(abs(typical$`% diff`) < 5))
```

# Virtual cohort

The paper's patients received a mix of regimens that is not tabulated per
patient, so the simulation covers the corners of the reported range: 20 or 40
mg/kg per dose every 8 or 12 h as a 1-h infusion, plus 20 mg/kg every 8 h as a
3-h infusion (the longest infusion used). Weight is drawn log-normally around the
Table 1 median of 1.58 kg with a spread matching its interquartile range. The
model has no covariates, so weight affects only the mg dose. Dosing runs for 48
h; with a half-life of about 2.3 h the last dosing interval is at steady state.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230315)
n_per_arm <- 200

arms <- tibble::tibble(
  treatment = c(
    "20 mg/kg q12h (1 h)", "20 mg/kg q8h (1 h)", "20 mg/kg q8h (3 h)",
    "40 mg/kg q12h (1 h)", "40 mg/kg q8h (1 h)"
  ),
  mgkg = c(20, 20, 20, 40, 40),
  tau_h = c(12, 8, 8, 12, 8),
  inf_h = c(1, 1, 3, 1, 1)
)

subjects <- arms[rep(seq_len(nrow(arms)), each = n_per_arm), ] |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    WT = 1.58 * exp(stats::rnorm(dplyr::n(), 0, log(2.04 / 1.30) / 1.349))
  )

t_end <- 48
doses <- subjects |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::reframe(
    id = id,
    time = seq(0, t_end - tau_h, by = tau_h),
    amt = mgkg * WT,
    rate = mgkg * WT / inf_h
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "central")

obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = subjects$id, time = seq(0, t_end, by = 0.1)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(subjects, id, treatment, tau_h, inf_h, WT), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, keep = c("treatment", "tau_h", "inf_h", "WT")) |>
  as.data.frame()

# Last dosing interval (steady state) for every subject.
last_int <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= t_end - tau_h - 1e-8) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - (t_end - tau_h))
```

```{r profiles, fig.cap = "Simulated steady-state meropenem concentrations over the last dosing interval (median and 5th-95th percentiles) by regimen. Dashed lines mark the EUCAST susceptible (2 mg/L) and resistant (8 mg/L) breakpoints used by the paper."}
last_int |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    med = stats::median(Cc),
    lo = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    hi = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(2, 8), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Meropenem (mg/L)")
```

# Peaks and troughs against the TDM observations

The paper reports geometric means of 23.5 mg/L for peaks (sampled within 30 min
after dosing) and 3.5 mg/L for troughs, pooled over all regimens. The cohort's
median daily dose at TDM, 94.3 mg/day at a median 1.58 kg, is about 60
mg/kg/day, which is the 20 mg/kg q8h regimen. The simulated peak is taken 15 min
after the end of the infusion, the middle of the paper's 30-min window.

```{r peak-trough}
pk_tr <- last_int |>
  dplyr::group_by(id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    peak = Cc[which.min(abs(tad - (inf_h[1] + 0.25)))],
    trough = Cc[which.max(tad)],
    .groups = "drop"
  )

gm_tab <- pk_tr |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Peak GM (mg/L)` = exp(mean(log(peak))),
    `Trough GM (mg/L)` = exp(mean(log(trough))),
    `Trough <= 2 mg/L (%)` = 100 * mean(trough <= 2),
    `Trough < 4 mg/L (%)` = 100 * mean(trough < 4),
    `Trough > 8 mg/L (%)` = 100 * mean(trough > 8),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
obs_row <- tibble::tibble(
  treatment = "Observed TDM (all regimens)",
  `Peak GM (mg/L)` = 23.5,
  `Trough GM (mg/L)` = 3.5,
  `Trough <= 2 mg/L (%)` = 19.7,
  `Trough < 4 mg/L (%)` = 50,
  `Trough > 8 mg/L (%)` = 9.1
)
dplyr::bind_rows(gm_tab, obs_row) |>
  dplyr::rename(Regimen = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated steady-state peaks and troughs vs. the observed TDM summary (Results).")

ref_arm <- gm_tab |> dplyr::filter(treatment == "20 mg/kg q8h (1 h)")
# The observed values pool regimens that are not tabulated, so this is an
# envelope: a wrong volume, rate constant or unit moves the geometric means
# several-fold, well outside a factor of 1.5.
stopifnot(
  ref_arm$`Peak GM (mg/L)` / 23.5 > 1 / 1.5, ref_arm$`Peak GM (mg/L)` / 23.5 < 1.5,
  ref_arm$`Trough GM (mg/L)` / 3.5 > 1 / 1.5, ref_arm$`Trough GM (mg/L)` / 3.5 < 1.5
)
```

# PKNCA validation

Steady-state NCA over the last dosing interval of each regimen. Table 2's
half-life median and the observed trough geometric mean are the only published
exposure values; the trough reference is attached to the 20 mg/kg q8h regimen,
which matches the cohort's median daily dose.

```{r pknca}
# A 0.25-h grid is ample for the interval NCA and keeps PKNCA fast.
conc_df <- last_int |>
  dplyr::filter(abs(tad * 4 - round(tad * 4)) < 1e-6) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
dose_df <- doses |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(subjects, id, treatment), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg")

intervals <- arms |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    treatment,
    start = t_end - tau_h,
    end = t_end,
    cmax = TRUE,
    cmin = TRUE,
    auclast = TRUE,
    half.life = TRUE
  )

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tibble::tibble(
  treatment = arms$treatment,
  half.life = 2.33,
  cmin = ifelse(arms$treatment == "20 mg/kg q8h (1 h)", 3.5, NA_real_)
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("half.life", "cmin"),
  units = c(half.life = "h", cmin = "mg/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. published values. * differs from reference by >20%.")
```

The simulated half-life reproduces the Table 2 median within a few percent in
every regimen, as it must for a linear model; the residual difference is the
terminal-phase point selection over a single dosing interval. The trough comparison is approximate: the observed 3.5
mg/L pools all regimens and infusion durations.

# PK/PD target attainment (Figures 3 and 4)

The paper evaluated the fraction of the dosing interval with unbound
concentration above the MIC (fT > MIC, unbound fraction 0.98) at MIC values of
1-32 mg/L, using each patient's Bayesian posterior parameters and actual
regimen, split by gestational age (< 32 vs >= 32 weeks). The population model has
no covariates, so it cannot separate the two GA groups; the simulated regimens
bracket them instead. Figure values below were read off the published bars and
lines by the maintainers.

```{r pta}
fu <- 0.98
mics <- c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32)

ft <- last_int |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, tad, Cc) |>
  tidyr::crossing(MIC = mics) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id, treatment, MIC) |>
  dplyr::summarise(fT = 100 * mean(fu * Cc > MIC), .groups = "drop")

pta_sim <- ft |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, MIC) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Median fT>MIC (%)` = stats::median(fT),
    `100% fT>MIC (% of patients)` = 100 * mean(fT >= 100),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

fig_ref <- tibble::tibble(
  MIC = mics,
  `Fig 3 median fT>MIC, GA < 32` = c(100, 100, 80, 52, 16, 0),
  `Fig 3 median fT>MIC, GA >= 32` = c(100, 100, 98, 68, 39, 0),
  `Fig 4 100% fT>MIC, GA < 32` = c(92, 75, 31, 8, 2, 0),
  `Fig 4 100% fT>MIC, GA >= 32` = c(100, 79, 57, 21, 7, 0)
)

pta_sim |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    id_cols = MIC,
    names_from = treatment,
    values_from = `100% fT>MIC (% of patients)`
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig_ref |> dplyr::select(MIC, dplyr::starts_with("Fig 4")), by = "MIC") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Percentage of patients with 100% fT > MIC: simulated regimens vs. Figure 4.")

pta_sim |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    id_cols = MIC,
    names_from = treatment,
    values_from = `Median fT>MIC (%)`
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig_ref |> dplyr::select(MIC, dplyr::starts_with("Fig 3")), by = "MIC") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Median fT > MIC (%): simulated regimens vs. Figure 3.")
```

```{r pta-plot, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Zyryanov 2023: percentage of patients achieving 100% fT > MIC. Lines are the simulated regimens; points are the published GA groups."}
fig4_long <- fig_ref |>
  dplyr::select(MIC, dplyr::starts_with("Fig 4")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-MIC, names_to = "group", values_to = "pct") |>
  dplyr::mutate(group = sub("Fig 4 100% fT>MIC, ", "Published ", group))

ggplot(pta_sim, aes(MIC, `100% fT>MIC (% of patients)`, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig4_long, aes(MIC, pct, shape = group), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = mics) +
  labs(x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "Patients with 100% fT > MIC (%)", colour = "Simulated", shape = NULL)
```

The published bars fall inside the band spanned by the simulated regimens at
every MIC from 2 to 32 mg/L, as expected for a cohort treated with a mix of
20-40 mg/kg doses every 8-12 h. At 1 mg/L the published 92% and 100% sit at or
just above the best simulated regimens (about 90%), whose log-normal tails
include a few patients with a very short half-life. The Figure 3 medians for the younger
group are close to the 20 mg/kg q8h 1-h regimen, the cohort's median daily
dose. The check below pins the band at the susceptible and resistant
breakpoints.

```{r pta-check}
band <- pta_sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(MIC) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    lo = min(`100% fT>MIC (% of patients)`),
    hi = max(`100% fT>MIC (% of patients)`),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig_ref, by = "MIC")
band_chk <- band |> dplyr::filter(MIC %in% c(2, 8))
# 10-point margin: the band edges are proportions from 200 simulated
# subjects, and the published bars are digitised group proportions.
stopifnot(
  all(band_chk$`Fig 4 100% fT>MIC, GA < 32` >= band_chk$lo - 10),
  all(band_chk$`Fig 4 100% fT>MIC, GA < 32` <= band_chk$hi + 10),
  all(band_chk$`Fig 4 100% fT>MIC, GA >= 32` >= band_chk$lo - 10),
  all(band_chk$`Fig 4 100% fT>MIC, GA >= 32` <= band_chk$hi + 10)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Non-parametric density approximated by log-normal marginals.** NPAG
  estimates a discrete joint distribution of support points (Figure 1 shows
  roughly 15 Kel and 15 V points). The model encodes independent log-normal
  marginals with the published medians and CV%; correlations between Kel and V
  are not reported and the multimodality visible in Figure 1 is not
  recoverable.
* **Medians as typical values.** The paper reports mean +/- SD (median) for Kel
  (0.31 +/- 0.13, median 0.3 1/h) and V (1.2 +/- 0.4, median 1.2 L). The medians
  are used because they reproduce the Table 2 derived medians (T1/2 2.33 h, CL
  0.355 L/h); the mean Kel would change the typical value by 3%.
* **Kel unit.** The Results sentence prints the Kel unit as 'L/h'; the
  Abstract's '1/h' is the correct unit for a rate constant and is used here.
* **Residual error not reported.** Observations were weighted by the inverse
  of the assay variance (a Pmetrics assay-error polynomial), but neither its
  coefficients nor a gamma or lambda term are given, and the article has no
  supplement. Both residual terms are therefore `fixed(0)`; simulated
  concentrations are individual predictions without measurement noise.
* **No covariates in the model.** Body weight, postconceptual age and Schwartz
  GFR were significant univariate predictors of the individual half-life and
  volume, but the paper reports no regression coefficients and states that
  multivariate analysis was not performed. These are documented in
  `covariatesDataExcluded`. Volume and clearance are absolute (L, L/h), so the
  model should be used only for patients resembling the 1.0-2.5 kg study cohort.
* **Regimens in the target-attainment comparison.** Per-patient regimens are
  not published, so the Figure 3 and 4 comparisons use bracketing regimens
  rather than the paper's patients, and the GA split cannot be reproduced.
